newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Colonial says share allocation to be cut.
newsitem.headline: Colonial says share allocation to be cut.

text.p: Colonial Ltd managing director Peter Smedley said the life insurance and banking group would have to reduce the number of shares allotted to each investor in its public offer.

Smedley said the offer of 153 million shares to public investors at A$2.60 each was now substantially oversubscribed, especially since the Australian Securities Commission (ASC) ordered on May 2 that the offer be re-opened until May 6.
Colonial, a Melbourne-based group with assets of A$38.4 billion, closed the public offer on April 28, four days ahead of the closing date in the prospectus, citing strong demand.

"We felt it was more appropriate for us to tell people when we did that we were oversubscribed and thereby not take people's cheques into the bank and avoid further disappointment," he told reporters after addressing the Securities Institute of Australia.
The individual allocation would be less than 1,000 shares, which had been the minimum subscription amount, Smedley said, but added that he did not know the final allocation number.
"I don't know, I really don't know. It is going to be less than 1,000. I think it would be unfair of me to make any pronouncements on that until I have seen the numbers."
The institutional bidding process for 115 million shares, based on an open price system, opens for two days from May 14.
Smedley said he had just finished an international roadshow which includes Hong Kong, Singapore, the United Kingdom, the United States, and New Zealand.
He said the institutional response has been pleasing.
He also said the bank had received 850 applications within two days of announcing on March 24 that it would introduce franchise banking around Australia.
Colonial owns the Colonial State Bank, which is based in Sydney, and ranks as the seventh largest bank in the nation.
